Task: On the Xiaomi account login page, clicking login POSTs to /serviceLogin a request whose password is sent as an uppercase MD5 `hash` field (e.g. 13819912565 becomes 9E2BFBE3D7050EDF876679FE5CE6E5AA). The bundle is string-array obfuscated (object keys appear as Qe([...]) decoder calls). Locate the anchor function for that hash field. The anchor function is the target-specific login param-builder on the submit->request chain: the single complete function whose own body assembles the account-login parameters object and binds the password hash into it — it runs the password through the md5 routine, uppercases the result and places it under the (decoded) hash key — rather than the md5 primitive it invokes to compute the digest (a generic crypto utility reached cross-file via module interop, not defined in this file), the string-array decoder that only reveals the obfuscated key names (an off-chain helper), or the request-sending sink. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do NOT return the md5 routine, the string-array decoder, or unrelated utilities — return the param-builder that binds the uppercase-MD5 hash into the login request. Only code under captures is in scope.  network_request POST /serviceLogin hash 13819912565 9E2BFBE3D7050EDF876679FE5CE6E5AA
